'''Harvey Akio Itano''' ({{langx|ja|板野 秋雄}},<ref>{{cite web | url=https://hojishinbun.hoover.org/?a=d&d=jan19420515-01.1.3&srpos=21&e=-------en-10--21--img-%e6%9d%bf%e9%87%8e------ | title=Nichibei Shinbun 1942.05.15 — Hoji Shinbun Digital Collection }}</ref> November 3, 1920 – May 8, 2010) was an American [[biochemist]] best known for his work on the molecular basis of [[sickle cell anemia]] and other diseases.  In collaboration with [[Linus Pauling]], Itano used [[electrophoresis]] to demonstrate the difference between normal [[hemoglobin]] and [[sickle cell hemoglobin]]; their 1949 paper "[[Sickle Cell Anemia, a Molecular Disease]]" (coauthored also with [[S. J. Singer]] and [[Ibert C. Wells]])<ref>{{Cite journal| volume = 110| issue = 2865| pages = 543–548| last = Pauling| first = Linus |author2=Harvey A. Itano |author3=S. J. Singer |author4=Ibert C. Wells | title = Sickle Cell Anemia, a Molecular Disease| journal = Science| date = 1949-11-01| bibcode = 1949Sci...110..543P| doi = 10.1126/science.110.2865.543| pmid = 15395398| s2cid = 31674765}}</ref> was a landmark in both [[molecular medicine]] and [[protein electrophoresis]], though the use of electrophoresis to separate hemoglobin variants had been pioneered by [[Maud Menten]] and collaborators some years earlier.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Andersch | first1 = M. A. | last2 = Wilson | first2 = D. A. | last3 = Menten | first3 = M. L. | year = 1944 | title = Sedimentation constants and electrophoretic mobilities of adult and fetal carbonylhemoglobin | journal = J. Biol. Chem. | volume = 153 | pages = 301–305 | doi = 10.1016/S0021-9258(18)51237-0 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

In 1979, Itano became the first [[Japanese American]] elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] (in the Genetics section).  Itano was an emeritus professor of [[pathology]] at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name="Lee">K. W. Lee.  "Remarkable Parents Who Raised Remarkable Family."  ''Sacramento Union'', June 25, 1979.  [http://www.itano.net/history/nichibei.htm Reprint from the ''Nichi Bei Times''] accessed August 25, 2008.</ref> In 2010, Itano died of complications from Parkinson's disease in La Jolla, California.<ref name=ucsdHealthSystem>{{cite web| title=In Memoriam: UC San Diego Pathology Professor Harvey Itano, MD, PhD, 1920-2010| url=http://health.ucsd.edu/news/2010/5-11-itano-obit.htm| access-date=2010-06-08| url-status=dead| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629194958/http://health.ucsd.edu/news/2010/5-11-itano-obit.htm| archive-date=2011-06-29}}</ref>

==Early life==
[[File:Sacramento, California. Harvey Akio Itano, 21, 1942 graduate from the University of California wher . . . - NARA - 537777.jpg|thumb|Recent UC Berkeley valedictorian Itano in an internment camp.]]
Itano was born in [[Sacramento, California]].  Itano attended the [[University of California, Berkeley]] where he was valedictorian of the Class of 1942.<ref name=doolittle>{{cite web | last = Doolittle | first = Russell F.|title=Biographical Memoirs: Harvey Itano 1920-2010|url=https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/itano-harvey.pdf| year=2014}}</ref>  However, due to [[Executive Order 9066]], Itano missed commencement in Berkeley after he and his family were sent to the [[Tanforan Assembly Center]], prior to being sent to the [[Tule Lake War Relocation Center|Tule Lake internment camp]].<ref name=weglyn>{{cite book |title=Years of Infamy: The Untold Story of America's Concentration Camps |publisher=William Morrow & Company |location=New York |last=Weglyn |first=Michi Nishiura |authorlink=Michi Weglyn|year=1976 |page=108|isbn=978-0688079963}}</ref>  Itano was later allowed to leave camp to attend the [[Saint Louis University (United States)|St. Louis University]] medical school, earning his M.D. in 1945.  He then went to graduate school at the [[California Institute of Technology]], where he received doctorates in chemistry and physics in 1950.<ref name=maughII>{{Cite news |last=Maugh II |first=Thomas H. |title=Harvey Itano dies at 89; researcher whose studies provided a breakthrough on sickle cell disease | newspaper=[[The Los Angeles Times]] |date=June 12, 2010 |url=http://www.latimes.com/features/health/la-me-harvey-itano-20100612,0,3417162.story }}</ref>

==Research==

While at Caltech, Itano joined the lab of [[Linus Pauling]] and began working on [[sickle cell anemia]], a genetic disease that Pauling was interested in.<ref name="Lee"/>  Pauling was convinced that sickle cell disease was caused by defective hemoglobin, and set Itano to find out what made sickle cell hemoglobin chemically different.<ref name="Goertzel">Ted Goertzel and Ben Goertzel.  ''Linus Pauling: A Life in Science and Politics''.  New York:BasicBooks, 1995.  p. 90</ref>  After failing with a number of other techniques, Itano succeeded in differentiating normal and sickle cell hemoglobins using [[moving boundary electrophoresis]].<ref name="Papers">"[http://libraries.ucsd.edu/speccoll/testing/html/mss0226a.html The Register of Harvey Itano Papers 1946 - 2000] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120614161412/http://libraries.ucsd.edu/speccoll/testing/html/mss0226a.html |date=2012-06-14 }}", MSS 0226, Mandeville Special Collections Library, Geisel Library, University of California, San Diego.  Accessed August 25, 2008.</ref>   He used an apparatus designed by [[Stanley M. Swingle]], a variation on the original apparatus of electrophoresis pioneer [[Arne Tiselius]].<ref>{{Cite journal| volume = 18| issue = 2| pages = 128–132| last = Swingle| first = Stanley M.| title = An Electrophoresis Apparatus Using Parabolic Mirrors| journal = Review of Scientific Instruments| access-date = 2008-08-25| date = February 1947| url = http://link.aip.org/link/?RSI/18/128/1| doi = 10.1063/1.1740898| pmid = 20288558| bibcode = 1947RScI...18..128S| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://archive.today/20120711003130/http://link.aip.org/link/?RSI/18/128/1| archive-date = 2012-07-11| url-access = subscription}}</ref>  He found that, under certain conditions, sickle cell hemoglobin is positively charged while normal hemoglobin is not, creating a difference in [[electrophoretic mobility]].<ref name="Goertzel"/>  By 1956, [[Vernon Ingram]] had determined that this was caused by a single difference in [[peptide sequence]],<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1038/178792a0| volume = 178| issue = 4537| pages = 792–794| last = Ingram| first = V. M.| title = A Specific Chemical Difference Between the Globins of Normal Human and Sickle-Cell Anaemia Haemoglobin| journal = Nature| date = 1956-10-13| pmid = 13369537|bibcode = 1956Natur.178..792I | s2cid = 4167855}}<!--| access-date = 2008-08-25--></ref> which by 1958 he determined to be a [[valine]] in the sickle cell mutant hemoglobin in place of [[glutamic acid]] in normal hemoglobin A.<ref>{{Cite journal| pmid = 13560404| volume = 28| issue = 3| pages = 539–45| last = Ingram| first = V M| title = Abnormal human haemoglobins. I. The comparison of normal human and sickle-cell haemoglobins by fingerprinting| journal = Biochimica et Biophysica Acta| date = June 1958| doi = 10.1016/0006-3002(58)90516-X}}<!--| access-date = 2008-08-25--></ref>

Itano's subsequent work brought the new field of "molecular medicine" to other genetic and blood diseases.  In 1954, he won the [[Eli Lilly Award]] in Biological Chemistry, and in 1972 he won the [[Martin Luther King Jr. Medical Achievement Award]], recognizing his sickle cell work.<ref name="Papers"/>
